target: UTM-bundled QEMU framework with HVF, virtio-ramfb, VirtIO keyboard/tablet, and WAV-backed VirtIO sound
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-exact-current-utm.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-psalmody-exact-current-utm.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody opened, recording was enabled, and H entered a C5 note.
WAV capture contains a sustained 50 ms tone at approximately 520 Hz (expected C5, 523.25 Hz) in three consecutive windows; each window has RMS amplitude about 6949 and peak 7000.
Shift+Escape exited playback, the graphical terminal evaluated 40+2 as 42, and zstatus reported failed=0.
The experimental audio timer delivered nine IRQs.
scope_note: This automated check uses UTM's bundled QEMU hardware profile; it verifies PCM output and app interaction in the emulated sound model. It does not substitute for confirming audible playback in the live UTM app. The generic long-effect WAV checker is not suitable for Psalmody's 260 ms note probe.
